sources.title: Stéphane Nonnenmacher, Introduction to Semiclassical Analysis, lecture notes (2019)
sources.locator: Full 83-page lecture-note PDF read. §1.1.2 printed p. 4 gives the scaled Fourier normalization; Definition 3.10 printed pp. 16–17 fixes Weyl quantization; Theorems 4.2 and 4.7 printed pp. 33–37 cover composition and Moyal expansion; Theorem 4.14 printed pp. 40–42 gives the Weyl Egorov/Duhamel route; Theorem 5.26 printed pp. 53–55 gives the bounded-symbol estimate.

contents.name: §1.1.2 p. 4: semiclassical Fourier transform normalization (2πℏ)^(-d/2)
contents.support: The source supplies the exact scaled transform formula; the unitary scaling from standard Plancherel is derived locally by the dilation operator.

contents.name: Definition 3.10 pp. 16–17: Weyl quantization convention
contents.support: The kernel convention is adopted; local coordinates and the [Q,P]=iε sign are stated explicitly.

contents.name: Theorem 5.26 pp. 53–55: order-zero Weyl boundedness by phase-space partition and almost orthogonality
contents.support: The proof is reconstructed locally by Gaussian packets and an integral-kernel Schur estimate, with the finite derivative count stated.

contents.name: Theorems 4.2 and 4.7 pp. 33–37: Weyl composition and Moyal expansion
contents.support: The Fourier-mode Weyl relation and Taylor remainder are proved locally with the page sign convention.

contents.name: Theorem 4.11 pp. 37–38: Weyl commutator expansion
contents.support: The source covers the Schwartz-symbol expansion; the unbounded kinetic-plus-potential symbol is treated by a separate local kernel Taylor proof.

contents.name: Theorem 4.14 pp. 40–42: finite-time Egorov theorem and Duhamel proof
contents.support: The Weyl O(ε²) route is used; operator-domain and smooth-potential hypotheses are made explicit locally.

contents.name: §3 Wigner discussion and the paper’s convention
contents.reason: The assigned marginals, reality, and explicit negative value are proved locally and the exact marginal proof is taken from Dell’Antonio’s lemma statement.

contents.name: Coherent-state and oscillator examples beyond the displayed local Gaussian calculation
contents.reason: The exact rotation and evolved distributional Wigner identity are proved locally from the exact quadratic Egorov theorem.

contents.name: First-excited-state negativity formula
contents.reason: The normalized oscillator state and its full Wigner polynomial are computed locally.

sources.title: Lawrence C. Evans and Maciej Zworski, Lectures on Semiclassical Analysis
sources.locator: Complete 231-page lecture-note PDF retrieved. Chapter 4, Theorems 4.15–4.17, printed pp. 64–68, treats the phase-space partition/Cotlar estimate and Weyl composition; Chapter 8 §8.2, Theorem 8.2, gives a weaker O(h) Egorov comparison.

contents.name: Theorems 4.15–4.16 pp. 64–67: bounded-symbol estimate via partition and almost orthogonality
contents.support: An independent treatment of the uniform order-zero bound; this pair gives its own complete finite-derivative proof.

contents.name: Theorem 4.17 pp. 67–68: composition and symbol expansion
contents.support: Independent comparison for the Weyl product; signs are recomputed from the local Fourier convention.

contents.name: Chapter 4 Weyl kernel convention
contents.support: Convention comparison; the source uses compatible Weyl midpoint quantization.

contents.name: Chapter 8 §8.2 Theorem 8.2: weak Egorov estimate of order O(h)
contents.reason: This source result does not establish the assigned Weyl O(ε²) estimate; it is recorded only as a scope comparison.

contents.name: Wigner marginal identities
contents.reason: The assigned marginal proof is local; the independently stated marginal result is in Dell’Antonio.

contents.name: Hilbert–Schmidt identity and explicit oscillator Wigner formulas
contents.reason: These statements are supplied locally and by the selected Dell’Antonio treatment.

contents.name: Quadratic-potential kernel Taylor proof and first-excited-state negativity polynomial
contents.reason: The extension beyond Schwartz symbols and the exact polynomial counterexample are proved locally.

sources.title: Gianfausto Dell’Antonio, Lectures on the Mathematics of Quantum Mechanics, Volume II: Selected Topics (2016)
sources.locator: Complete 386-page lecture-note PDF retrieved. Lecture 1 §1 printed pp. 15–20 covers Wigner definition, reality/marginals (Lemma 1.2), and coherent Gaussian states; Lecture 2 §2.2 printed pp. 41–47 covers Weyl kernels, Hilbert–Schmidt norm and the boundedness outline; §§2.5–2.6 printed pp. 50–54 discuss Moyal products, commutators and dynamics.

contents.name: Lecture 1 §1 pp. 15–18: Wigner definition, reality and the two marginal formulas (Lemma 1.2)
contents.support: The source states the marginals but omits their proof; the full Fubini/Fourier proof and negativity check are supplied locally.

contents.name: Lecture 1 §1 pp. 18–20: coherent-state Gaussian in phase space
contents.support: The initial coherent Gaussian Wigner density is independently compared; exact quadratic time transport is proved locally.

contents.name: Lecture 2 §2.2 pp. 41–43: Weyl kernels and Hilbert–Schmidt norm
contents.support: The local proof computes the exact scaled Fourier kernel norm and the resulting bounded extension.

contents.name: Lecture 2 §2.2 pp. 43–47: bounded-symbol theorem and phase-space partition outline
contents.support: Independent treatment of the operator bound; the complete coherent-state almost-orthogonality estimate is proved locally.

contents.name: Lecture 2 §§2.5–2.6 pp. 50–54: Weyl products, commutators and Heisenberg dynamics
contents.support: The source motivates the local Fourier-mode expansion and Duhamel argument; the exact remainder bounds are proved in this batch.

contents.support: The Weyl/Wigner midpoint and Fourier normalizations are compared against the local convention.

contents.name: Independent bounded derivative count for the CV estimate

contents.name: First-excited-state Wigner negativity polynomial
contents.reason: The entire normalized Hermite-state calculation and negativity disk are derived locally.
